title: Hybrid burst+steady-state load generator and long-duration soak for Dedicated pools
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Goal: Build and run a reproducible hybrid load harness that combines long-duration steady-state traffic with periodic controlled bursts to validate Dedicated pool autoscaling behavior and detect p95/regression drift. This ticket covers generator implementation, harness orchestration, metric collection, and integration with our regression detector pipeline.

Background: Existing soak runs exercise steady throughput but do not emulate real-world burstiness (e.g., interleaved short spikes from user traffic) and tenant-mix effects. We've also seen occasional p95 latency drift after kernel selection changes; we need a repeatable test that surfaces regressions quickly.

Requirements and design decisions:
- Workload model: 2-hour steady-state window at target tokens/sec plus 3-minute Poisson-mode bursts every 20 minutes. Steady targets: 200k tokens/sec aggregate for the pool (configurable). Burst target: additional 80-120k tokens/sec injected over 3 minute window.
- Client mix: 70% short-chat (avg 40 tokens/request), 30% long-generation (avg 600 tokens/request) to stress KV cache and batching.
- Latency SLOs and thresholds: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 200ms under steady-state; p95 < 350ms during burst windows.
- Regression detection rules: flag run as failing when (a) p95 increases > 20% vs baseline or (b) sustained tokens/sec drops > 10% for > 5 minutes while CPU/GPU utilization unchanged.
- Metrics to collect: tokens/sec, request/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, bundle-level GPU utilization, queue length, batching efficiency (tokens/request_batch), KV cache hit ratio, GC/paging events, and model kernel fallback counts.
- Harness properties: deterministic seed for payload selection, configurable tenant IDs to test multi-tenant interference, ability to replay recorded real-traffic traces, and ramp-up/warm-up window (15 minutes) to populate KV caches.
- Automation: runs scheduled via CI job (ci/perf/dedicated-hybrid-soak) that provisions a dedicated test cluster (infra-qa-dedicated-XX), deploys target model variant (pinned), runs harness, gathers metrics to perf-bucket, triggers grafana dashboard snapshot, and posts results to regression detector API.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Hybrid load generator service and CLI implemented and validated against a local staging pool.
2) A full 12-hour soak run executes end-to-end in the QA Dedicated environment, with artifacts: prom tarball, grafana snapshots, and regression-detector report.
3) Alerts and detection: Prometheus rule and alerting group created to surface the two regression conditions; alerts route to #perf-alerts and create an automatic issue when tripped.
4) Documentation: Confluence runbook describing config knobs, expected baseline numbers, and troubleshooting steps.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Hybrid+Soak+and+Burst+Harness
- Prototype repo (generator): https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/tree/eng-11024-hybrid
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/78 (initial generator)
- Regression detector API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/regression-detector/pull/210
- Example Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.cloud/d/dedicated/perf-hybrid-soak?orgId=1

Operational notes and constraints:
- We must reserve a Dedicated test pool for the duration of the 12 hour soak; current quota requires scheduling with infra. Blocker: infra-qa-owners must approve reservation (ticket INFRA-602).
- Running long soaks increases infra spend; we will limit runs to weekdays during low business usage and retain artifacts for 30 days.
- To avoid noisy signals, the harness will run a calibration step to set steady tokens/sec based on observed max sustainable throughput for the pinned model on the test pool.

Open questions: 
- Should we include a cold-start burst (all caches empty) at the beginning of each run to validate cold-path performance separately? (proposal: one short cold-burst pre-run flag).
- How many tenant permutations should we test in a single run vs separate runs to isolate multi-tenant interference?

Next steps: 
- (Ethan) complete CLI & Poisson burst injector + tenant-mix config by 2026-02-18.
- (Marisol) schedule infra reservation with INFRA-602 and confirm dedicated cluster specs.
- Create CI job and hook regression-detector integration.
